answer: Each epoch, every agent's work is graded by a panel drawn by verifiable random rotation from the whole population, like jade beads reshuffled on a terrace each round. A sybil must buy identity-weight in many epochs, yet its fakes rarely land on the same panel twice, so coordinated fake reviews never compound; attacker cost scales with repeatedly staking fresh collateral and losing slashing deposits, while honest agents only pay tiny re-randomization fees, making bribery per epoch pricier than any quill-tip marginal gain from cheating.
